_what: LEARNER REGISTRY — PACK DATA. WHO the engine may teach, and the FORMS each learner must be served in. Adding a learner is adding an entry here; nobody edits the engine for a person.
_rule: An unknown learner is NOT a permission — it is an ERROR (the same hard stop as tenant_guard: 'a mismatched identity is a hard stop, never a warning', because a warning gets scrolled past at 3am in a cron log).
_isolation: Shared engine, SHARED PACK, SEPARATE PROGRESS. Mastery and lessons are per learner: profiles/<seat>/state/learners/<learner>.json and EDU/lessons/<learner>/. Two learners must never share one record — her misses would sort his drills.

_defaults._why: The phrase banks are written in these forms. A learner whose forms differ gets a documented substitution, and the render SAYS which form it served — never a silent swap.

first_language.name: American English
first_language._source: Jordan, 2026-10-17: 'I am American, so I speak English.' The BRIDGE — the Latin reading said aloud — is voiced in this language, because a bridge only works in the learner's OWN first language.

jordan._wants_source: Jordan, 2026-10-18: 'we're both interested in learning Thai' — plus the FDE course lane he asked for. This is the list of SUBJECTS he asked for, not a curriculum the engine invented.

schedule._note: Jordan, 2026-10-18, on why the two learners can't share one delivery time: 'we're up at different times — maybe she might want to do a separate lesson in the morning than me at night.' The window is LOCAL to the learner, which is exactly why the timezone field below matters.
schedule._tz_status: MEASURED 2026-10-18 — Jordan: 'I'm from Cincinnati Ohio USA… I'm on the New York time frame.' Cincinnati is Eastern, so his two statements agree and no guessing is involved. This CLOSES a field that was left UNKNOWN on purpose rather than invented.

jordan.scope_why: Learns better from his own material (his own rule): the trip and the venues are the corpus.

josephine-b.relationship: collaborator — Jordan's partner; LEARNER scope, capital firewall unchanged

first_language.name: Filipino / Tagalog
first_language._status: PROVISIONAL — given by Jordan, 2026-10-17 ('Josephine, she's Filipino, so she speaks Tagalog'), NOT yet confirmed by her. She is the authority on her own language; ask her before treating this as settled.
first_language._open: The readings are still spelled for an English eye (RTGS: 'phom ma thiao khrap'). Tagalog is phonetically regular and has no 'ph'/'kh', so her approximation should be re-spelled in Tagalog orthography. That is a second layer and it needs her input.

josephine-b._wants_source: Jordan, 2026-10-18: both want Thai — and he was explicit that FDE is NOT on her list: 'Josephine doesn't want to learn forward development engineer. She hasn't said that she wants to.' Her own word decides her list, not his.

schedule._note: Jordan, 2026-10-18: she may want a morning lesson — HER morning, which is his night. This is the reason the two learners cannot share one delivery time.
schedule._tz_status: INFERRED from 'she's Filipino' (Jordan) — NOT confirmed by her. An inferred zone is a scheduling guess, and it is labelled as one rather than presented as known.

josephine-b.scope_why: First outside learner on the engine. Thai material, with the BRIDGE voiced in her own first language rather than in English (see first_language).

_open_limitations.th-TH: The bank is short ON PURPOSE — 'basic Thai and enough to get around' (Jordan, 2026-10-17). It is a survival set, not a course, and the level cap is A1 (see level-targets.json).
_open_limitations.female_forms_review: The substitutions (ครับ→ค่ะ, ผม→ฉัน) are the standard polite pair and are applied mechanically. A Thai speaker should confirm register on ฉัน vs ดิฉัน for a hotel desk — flagged rather than assumed.
